newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares buoyant in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares buoyant in active trade.

text.p: Nigerian shares ended buoyantly on Friday on strong blue-chip gains, dealers said.
The all-share index rose 18.28 points to 6,501.89 from 6,483.61 on Thursday.
An impressive full year result by conglomerate PZ Industries also cheered the market, but its merger proposal with an associated company meant a technical suspension on its price.
"Based on their half-year and nine-month results, I would say it was in line with the market's expectation," trader James Odife told Reuters.
PZ's after-tax profit was 1.38 billion naira in the year to end-May from 796.45 million naira the period last year.
Strong interest persisted in cement, construction, food and oil, as was the case all week, keeping share prices up.
Unipetrol consolidated on its impressive gain in the past two weeks, closing 30 kobo up at 39.30 naira. National Oil rose similarly to end the week at 30.70 naira.

Benue Cement was the sector's leader on Friday, adding 25 kobo to 5.25 naira. West African Portland Cement followed with 23 kobo at 32.22 naira. Construction firm Cappa and D'Alberto also soared to 8.25 naira, up 26 kobo.

Flour Mills led food shares with 15 kobo to close at 10.65 naira, while Cadbury and Union Dicon Salt added 10 kobo apiece to 26.30 naira and 34.20 naira, respectively. Nigerian Bottling rose nine kobo to 28.59 naira, while Nigerian Tobacco continued to rebound, ending three up at 2.79 naira.
Traders said blue chips would remain attractive, but investors in healthcare and construction shares looked promising in the next couple of weeks.

"Healthcare companies and construction firms are marked for growth because of PTF (Petroleum Trust Fund) money they have just received," one trader said. The fund was created in 1994 by the military government to cushion the effect of a four-fold rise in fuel prices by investing in public causes.
While traders saw insurance firms as attractive because they were stabilising after a period of distress, they said packaging shares would be on the downward trend for sometime.
"Their products are consumed by manufacturers whose warehouses are full of unsold goods," said Chuks Ohanwusi of Networth Securities.
Carnaud Metal Box shed six kobo to 4.04 naira, Avon Crowncaps lost four kobo at 4.44 naira and Studio Press was two down at 1.12 naira. ($1= 80 naira)
